news.originalContent:
(Photos by Finn Gomez/Getty Images/Al Drago/Getty Images)

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise and Republican Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan launched their bids Wednesday to become their party’s next leader after losing the majority.

House Speaker Mike Johnson announced he would not seek a leadership role after Democrats regained the majority in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Scalise and Jordan will face off on Tuesday seeking to become the minority leader in the 120th Congress.

“To succeed in this fight, we will need to stand united as one team, be smart and strategic to secure conservative policy wins where we can, closely coordinate our defense against aggressive oversight and together develop a clear vision and agenda to earn back the majority in 2028,” Scalise said. “That is why I’m running to be your Republican Leader—I am ready to lead on day one and chart our path back to the majority.” (RELATED: House Democrats Retake Majority As Voters Punish GOP For Inflation, Iran War)

🚨🚨 @SteveScalise officially announces he will run to be the next Republican leader @DailyCaller https://t.co/ZZiH3NgAHj

Scalise stated that he helped deliver major wins for his party, including the Working Families Tax Cuts, and fought against “far-left Democrat bills.” He also planned to work on discrediting Democrats’ potential investigations into President Donald Trump and his administration.

“House Democrats are about to unleash the most radical ‘oversight’ agenda we have seen in years. Yes, they will seek to impeach President Trump, but their focus will extend far beyond the Oval Office. They have made clear they will undertake a comprehensive approach that will target President Trump’s family, key cabinet officials, and any ally who has supported our America First agenda, including outside conservative partners and industry leaders,” Scalise continued. “Make no mistake: they will weaponize every single gavel.”

“Through close coordination with the administration and our committee leaders, we will deploy a comprehensive approach that involves all committees to discredit their ‘investigations’ and put them on defense,” the majority leader said.

Scalise was elected as House majority whip in 2014 and served as House minority whip from 2019 to 2022. He became House majority leader in 2023. A gunman seriously injured Scalise after a would-be assassin attacked lawmakers practicing for the annual congressional baseball game in 2017.

Jordan said in his “Dear Colleague” letter that he understands the “Democrats’ playbook” and called on the conference to stand united in fighting against them.

“There is far more that unites us as Republicans than divides us,” Jordan wrote. “We all believe America is worth fighting for. We are optimistic that America’s best days are ahead and that through God’s grace, we can overcome any obstacle. With your help, I will use every minute of the next two years working to advance our Republican priorities and restore our majority.”

Jordan, a former wrestling coach, has chaired the House Judiciary Committee since Jan. 3, 2023.

Scalise and Jordan ran for speaker after the House ousted former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in October 2023, although neither received the votes to assume the role. Jordan became the nominee after defeating Scalise in an internal party vote, but lost three consecutive votes after facing opposition from moderate Republicans.

Jordan is a founding member of the House Freedom Caucus, which was often a thorn in the side for Johnson. Members of the Freedom Caucus, including Republican Texas Rep. Chip Roy, voted against a rule in September to protest the passage of the continuing resolution (CR) particularly because it delayed a ban on hemp THC products. Two Democrats rescued Johnson during that vote from facing a floor shutdown.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is expected to become the next speaker. He could face opposition from members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) over issues such as Medicare for All and Israel aid.
news.content:
(عکس های فین گومز/گتی ایماژ/آل دراگو/گتی ایماژ)
استیو اسکالیز، رهبر اکثریت مجلس نمایندگان و جیم جردن، نماینده جمهوری‌خواه اوهایو، روز چهارشنبه پس از از دست دادن اکثریت، پیشنهادهای خود را برای رهبری بعدی حزب خود آغاز کردند. مایک جانسون، رئیس مجلس نمایندگان، پس از اینکه دموکرات‌ها اکثریت را در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای روز سه‌شنبه به دست آوردند، اعلام کرد که به دنبال نقش رهبری نخواهد بود. اسکالیس و اردن روز سه‌شنبه به‌دنبال تبدیل شدن به رهبر اقلیت در کنگره 120 هستند. «برای موفقیت در این مبارزه، باید به‌عنوان یک تیم متحد باشیم، هوشمندانه و استراتژیک باشیم تا بتوانیم پیروزی‌های سیاست محافظه‌کاران را تا جایی که می‌توانیم تضمین کنیم، دفاع خود را از نزدیک در برابر نظارت تهاجمی هماهنگ کنیم و با هم یک چشم‌انداز و دستور کار روشن برای بازگرداندن اکثریت در 202 ایجاد کنیم.» "به همین دلیل است که من برای رهبری جمهوری خواه شما نامزد می شوم - من آماده هستم که در روز اول رهبری کنم و مسیر خود را به سمت اکثریت ترسیم کنم." (مرتبط: دموکرات های مجلس نمایندگان اکثریت را بازپس می گیرند زیرا رای دهندگان جمهوری خواه را به دلیل تورم، جنگ ایران مجازات می کنند)
🚨🚨 @SteveScalise رسما اعلام کرد که برای رهبری بعدی جمهوریخواهان نامزد خواهد شد @DailyCaller https://t.co/ZZiH3NgAHj اسکالیس اظهار داشت که به پیروزی‌های بزرگی برای حزبش، از جمله کاهش مالیات خانواده‌های کارگر، کمک کرده و با «لایحه‌های چپ افراطی دموکرات‌ها» مبارزه کرده است. او همچنین قصد داشت روی بی‌اعتبار کردن تحقیقات احتمالی دموکرات‌ها در مورد رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ و دولتش کار کند. «دموکرات‌های مجلس نمایندگان آمریکا در آستانه راه‌اندازی رادیکال‌ترین دستور کار «نظارت» است که در سال‌های اخیر دیده‌ایم. بله، آنها خواهند کرد.

news.originalContent:
Vice President JD Vance broke his silence after Democrats swept the midterms, admitting the real reason Republicans endured the bruising defeat.

Vance outlined the main issues that animated voters, including the cost of living, America’s relationship with Israel, ending the war with Iran, and putting America first.

The through line, Vance admits, is that Republicans lost because President Donald Trump started a war with Iran. (RELATED: Trump Brought Back America First — The Daily Caller Is Taking On The Establishment Trying To Hijack It)

“In the next few months, there’s going to be a lot of gaslighting,” Vance said in a Wednesday post on X. “Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement — by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you.”

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance added. “The president himself said so last night.”

One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we’re going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us." Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026. There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were: 1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.) In the next few months, there’s going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there. I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

As of this writing, Democrats have flipped seven Senate seats and over two dozen House seats. States like Texas and Kansas, once considered Republican strongholds, were swept by Democrats. Republicans in Iowa, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, and South Carolina also suffered bruising defeats.

Some political operatives in the GOP have already begun to suggest that the devastating loss was because of a “foreign op”; Vance carved his own path forward. (RELATED: ‘No Downside’: Iran War Hawks Get Midterm Reality Check)

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” Vance said. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

“I remain hopeful about our country,” Vance continued. “To the people who are pissed off and want to say, ‘I told you so’: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.”

news.originalContent:
Illustration by Daily Caller Staff; with Getty Images

Hey y’all, welcome back to Unfit to Print.

We’re doing something a little bit different today.

CONSERVATISM AT A CROSSROADS

Republicans just lost both chambers of Congress, and the party has some serious soul-searching to do.

President Donald Trump has been the center of Republican politics for more than a decade.

He shattered the old GOP consensus on immigration, trade, foreign policy, and the relationship between the party and working-class Americans.

But identifying the failures of the party is not the same thing as building a durable political movement to replace it.

There’s an important distinction between MAGA and America First. MAGA is a movement built around Trump. America First is a governing philosophy that predates him and ought to outlast him. Trump may have brought those principles back into the political mainstream, but he doesn’t have a monopoly on defining them.

The conservative movement now faces an important question: What does America First actually mean beyond Trump? And who gets to set the agenda?

You may think these questions are premature. Trump is staring down a lame-duck presidency, but he still has at least two years as the de facto leader of the party. He’ll also have a major say in who inherits his political mantle in 2028.

My former boss Geoffrey Ingersoll, however, once said something really important about political media and the Daily Caller’s role in it: “It’s like pursuing a football on the football field. You want to go to where it’s going. You don’t want to go to where it is.”

That philosophy has stuck with me, and it’s a big part of how I think about my job as editor-in-chief.

The Daily Caller’s responsibility isn’t just to cover whoever is feuding on the Hill, what bill is being introduced in Congress, where the president’s next rally is going to be, or even who won the midterms.

Our job is to identify and cover the issues, ideas, and tensions that are going to shape American politics — and your lives — in the future, without waiting for permission from Washington’s political establishment.

That approach has ruffled some feathers.

Semafor published a piece Sunday about the Daily Caller’s editorial direction under my leadership, titled “More MAGA than MAGA: How the Daily Caller turned on MAGA and Trump.”

The article focused heavily on our coverage of the war with Iran, Israeli influence in Washington, and the backlash we’ve received for daring to question uniparty orthodoxy.

I spoke to the author of the article for about 45 minutes. He included just one of my quotes: “The Iran war is a huge turning point for the conservative movement.”

But the reporter didn’t include anything I said after that.

What I explained is that the war is exposing tensions within the MAGA coalition that have existed since Trump first brought it together.

Trump’s coalition shared a distrust of Washington, resentment toward the political class, and a desire to put American interests first. But beneath that broad agreement were competing ideas about the role of government, the economy, foreign policy, and the relationship between ordinary Americans and powerful institutions.

For years, Trump’s personality helped paper over those differences.

Now, those disagreements are coming to a head.

For years, Trump railed against forever wars and promised to put American interests first. Now the United States is stuck in another quagmire in the Middle East, and conservatives are confronting fundamental disagreements about what the America First approach is to military intervention, foreign alliances, our obligations to other countries, and the impact on Americans’ pocketbooks.

Meanwhile, young Americans are struggling to find jobs, afford homes, get married, and start families. American workers are confronting the consequences of legal and illegal immigration, artificial intelligence and automation, and an economy that’s increasingly dominated by powerful corporations. The proliferation of online pornography and gambling is raising serious questions about addiction, socialization, and community. Americans also remain suspicious of government surveillance, censorship, and the influence of wealthy donors and special interests.

And we’re taking a particularly hard look at foreign influence in Washington, whether it’s coming from Israel, China, or any other country seeking to shape American policy. The question isn’t whether we consider a particular nation a friend or an adversary. It’s whether its interests are being placed ahead of those of the American people.

These are precisely the issues we’ve been putting front and center at the Daily Caller.

Frankly, I don’t think the question should be why we’re covering these issues. It should be why more conservative media outlets aren’t.

Semafor describes us as “more MAGA than MAGA,” but that misses the point. We’re not competing for the title of Trump’s most faithful disciples. We’re asking hard questions about whether the movement that promised to shake up Washington is actually changing it — or simply replacing one set of powerful interests with another.

Our slogan is “Your Rebels in the Swamp.”

“Your” refers to our readers — the American people.

“Rebels” means we don’t toe the partisan line or adopt narratives just because they’re popular or convenient.

And “the Swamp” signals that we are in the heart of Washington, reporting the truth just blocks from the White House.

This rebellious spirit goes back to our founding. When political media was largely dominated by liberal cable outlets and progressive digital blogs, our founders had a vision for a new kind of conservative publication — one that would challenge the prevailing media narratives, break stories the establishment press ignored, and have a little fun while doing it.

That didn’t just apply to Democrats. One of the Caller’s first big scoops exposed the Republican National Committee’s (RNC) nearly $2,000 expenditure at a bondage-themed Hollywood nightclub.

Our commitment to the truth doesn’t change depending on who occupies the seats of power in the nation’s capital. Neither does our willingness to make powerful people uncomfortable.

And frankly, anyone who thought otherwise wasn’t paying attention.

So the online chatter that the Daily Caller is going through some sort of radical transformation has got it wrong. We’re not pivoting. We’re recommitting.

I haven’t seen our newsroom this excited about its mission in years. Our reporters know exactly what we’re trying to accomplish, and they’re fearless in pursuing the stories that matter.

That’s what a newsroom with a clear sense of purpose looks like.

I don’t expect everyone to agree with every story we publish.

In fact, over the past few months, we’ve increasingly been accused of being foreign-funded puppets, haters, or controlled opposition by folks who mistakenly viewed us as a member of their “team.”

So let me be clear now about whose team we are on:

Which brings me back to yesterday’s election results.

There will be no shortage of people assigning blame, questioning what went wrong, and declaring themselves or their faction the future of the party.

We can’t let those debates obscure the more important point:

What is the conservative movement actually trying to conserve, and what kind of country is it trying to build?

Is keeping the left out of power enough, or do we have a positive vision for America that leaves our children and grandchildren something worthwhile to inherit?

The Daily Caller isn’t interested in anointing Trump’s successor or pretending we have all the answers.

But we are going to make sure Washington can’t ignore the voices of ordinary Americans.

It would be a dereliction of duty to let the next chapter of conservatism be written exclusively by politicians, wealthy donors, consultants, and the loudest voices on social media.

The people who have to live with the consequences deserve a say, too.

To read more articles like this, please become a Substack subscriber.

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

news.originalContent: Senior government officials admit that Israel's public opinion in the international community "has never been worse." According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten.  Follow Ynetnews on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | TikTok >> More stories: IDF releases name of fallen soldier in West Bank terror attack UN chief in Rafah crossing says world 'seen enough' of Gaza war Two Air Force pilots reminisce about their murdered brothers: 'There's no room for pain in the air' The officials added that the intensity of accusations made against Israel only increases, and attempts to equate Hamas's actions in Israel are being made, with allegations accusing IDF soldiers of sexually harassing Palestinian prisoners. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

Ynetnews را در فیس بوک و توییتر دنبال کنید >> مطالب مرتبط: اسراییل نام دو خواهر کشته شده در حمله تروریستی کرانه باختری را اعلام کرد حداقل یک کشته و شش زخمی در حمله تروریستی در تل آویو خانواده دو دختر خود را در حمله تروریستی مرگبار از دست دادند اعضای جامعه یهودی لندن از جمله دوستان خانواده که پس از پایان شبات از اخبار ویرانگر شنیده بودند، تنها در آن زمان با گزارش های وحشتناک ری از مرگ مواجه شدند. مراسم تشییع پیکر خواهران دی امروز در قبرستان کفار اتزیون برگزار می شود.   خاخام لئو دی به عنوان دستیار خاخام در کنیسه هندون یونایتد در شمال لندن از سال 2008 تا 2011، و به عنوان خاخام ارشد در کنیسه رادلت یونایتد از سال 2011 تا 2014 خدمت کرد، پس از آن خانواده به عنوان الیه درآمدند. آنها خانواده ای بسیار محبوب و مورد احترام در جامعه یهودیان بریتانیا بودند. «مردم احساس شوک و ناامیدی می کنند. خانواده مردمی جمعی بودند و به جوامع خود به خوبی خدمت می کردند و مورد پسند بودند.» یکی از اعضای سابق جماعت کنیسه یونایتد هندون که نمی خواست نامش فاش شود، گفت.  من از دیدن این احساس بدم می‌آید... آدم‌های خوبی که هرگز به کسی صدمه نمی‌زنند، به قتل رسیده‌اند. من می توانم

news.originalContent: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guards warned anti-government protesters of "decisive" action if unrest over gasoline price hikes do not cease, state television reported on Monday. The warning appeared to hint at a looming crackdown on protests that flared nationwide in response to an official announcement on Friday of gasoline rationing and price hikes of at least 50 percent. "If necessary we will take decisive and revolutionary action against any continued moves to disturb the people's peace and security," the Guards said in a statement carried by state media.
news.content: تلویزیون دولتی روز دوشنبه گزارش داد که سپاه پاسداران قدرتمند ایران به معترضان ضد دولتی هشدار داد که اگر ناآرامی ها بر سر افزایش قیمت بنزین متوقف نشود، اقدام «قاطعانه» خواهند کرد. به نظر می‌رسد این هشدار به سرکوب اعتراض‌هایی که در سراسر کشور در واکنش به اعلام رسمی روز جمعه مبنی بر سهمیه‌بندی بنزین و افزایش حداقل 50 درصدی قیمت‌ها شعله‌ور شد، اشاره می‌کند. سپاه پاسداران در بیانیه‌ای که توسط رسانه‌های دولتی منتشر شد، گفت: «در صورت لزوم، در برابر هرگونه اقدام مستمر برای برهم زدن آرامش و امنیت مردم، اقدام قاطع و انقلابی خواهیم کرد».
